issues.description: Field 'animals' in class de.tum.cit.ase.Farm: the problem statement and UML require the Farm to aggregate animals using a List<Animal> and to initialize that List with a new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor; the solution implementation instead declares the field as Queue<Animal>, initializes it with new LinkedList<>(), and exposes a getter returning Queue<Animal>. This type-level mismatch (List/ArrayList vs Queue/LinkedList) between the specification and the provided solution changes the expected API and semantics and will confuse students about which collection type they must use and which getter/setter signatures to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the solution to declare the field as private List<Animal> animals; initialize it in the no-arg constructor with this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); and change the getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>. Alternatively, if the exercise intends to teach Queue/LinkedList semantics, update the problem statement, UML, and template instructions to explicitly allow/require Queue<Animal> backed by LinkedList. The first option (align solution to List/ArrayList) preserves the current textual requirements and UML.
